Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1005 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.
  • If, in response to nationwide protests, the government prepares to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.
  • France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.

If, in response to nationwide protests, the government prepares to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.

France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP). By comparison, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio is roughly 65%, despite its €600 billion investment package for infrastructure and defense.

Germany still enjoys the highest possible AAA credit rating. France, by contrast, is rated AA, A+ or Aa3, depending on the credit agency. While Germany's outlook is consistently rated as stable, several agencies have assigned France a negative outlook.

Recent findings suggest that as a result, the French government must pay higher interest rates on its borrowing than Berlin. The risk premium over German government bonds, known as the spread, is now at its highest level since the financial crisis. France pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest than Germany on 10-year bonds.

The spread acts as a kind of "fever gauge" for bond markets, explained Friedrich Heinemann, an economist at the Leibniz Center for European Economic Research (ZEW) in Mannheim.

Recent findings suggest that "This fever gauge then forces a change of course. If the spread rises too sharply, France's financing conditions come under pressure, and anyone in France who needs a loan has to pay higher interest rates. Banks then get into trouble, and the crisis escalates further," Heinemann told DW.

"This could then slide toward a financial crisis, which would finally send a clear signal to everyone: Things cannot continue like this unless you are prepared to risk a genuine economic collapse," he said.

Landry Charrier, a researcher at the University of Bonn's Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies, however, does not expect France's debt-fueled spending spree to end anytime soon.

"French people are aware of the country's high public debt. But debt remains an abstract concept if its consequences are barely felt in everyday life. According to INSEE [the French national statistics agency — Editor's note], 56% of the population receive more in government benefits and services than they pay in taxes and social contributions. The majority therefore have a tangible interest in maintaining the status quo," Charrier told DW.

Industry observers note that for more than half a century, France has regularly spent more than it collects in tax revenue. The last time it balanced its national budget was in 1974.

According to recent reports, france last paid a similarly high-risk premium at the end of 2011, during the eurozone debt crisis. What is particularly striking is how swiftly it has risen: Since June 2026, the spread over German government bonds has more than doubled.

Recent findings suggest that the main driver is not so much the general level of interest rates. Rather, it's the growing risk premium investors demand in response to high debt levels, political instability, large budget deficits and the recent unrest.

According to recent reports, the higher the interest rates, the larger the share of the national budget that must be devoted to debt servicing alone. France is expected to pay more than €79 billion in interest on its total public debt in 2026. That figure is projected to exceed €91 billion in 2027 and could reach between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030.

In a recent development, these figures include the costs incurred by social security funds and local authorities. The central government's interest bill alone is at the moment estimated at €62.6 billion by the Agence France Tresor, a French Treasury agency.

In the coming years, France will have to refinance large amounts of outstanding bonds that were issued when interest rates were at historic lows. At the same time, the country's substantial budget deficit means it must take on additional debt.

According to recent reports, the trend of rising interest costs is also affecting Germany. The ZEW's Heinemann has calculated that German interest payments are likely to increase sharply by the early 2030s.

"For the federal government alone, which has so far paid around €30 billion, the figure will triple within a few years as both debt and interest rates rise. And it won't stop there — it will exceed €90 billion. Reaching €100 billion in annual interest payments in the federal budget is then no longer far off," warned the economist.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that in France, however, economic realities seem to have little impact on political debate. Both the far-right National Rally (RN) and the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) are campaigning on costly promises.

RN leader Marine Le Pen, for example, wants to reinstate the retirement age of 62 while promising €140 billion in savings. Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's leader, has even suggested that government bonds held by the French central bank should be "thrown into the fire.".

"Nobody will ever notice they've disappeared," he has claimed.

For Heinemann, this is "a good example of radical parties on both the right and the left simply telling economic fairy tales.".

Their common message, he said, is that "there is a way out of this mess that requires neither fiscal consolidation nor painful cuts.".

Charrier is convinced that many French people have yet to grasp the seriousness of the situation.

"The euro has made it easier for France to access cheap financing and has long softened the pressure to adjust," he pointed out.

Industry observers note that "In the past, currency devaluations [of the French franc — Editor's note] made economic imbalances immediately felt through declining purchasing power and rising prices. Today, that warning signal is missing. This has created the illusion that necessary adjustments can be postponed indefinitely," Charrier said.

This article was originally written in German.

All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5912 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 newly introduced players, but did not upgrade two of the most vital positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Industry observers note that zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Sources indicate that suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

According to recent reports, spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Industry observers note that asked if Tottenham had made a substantial mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi stated: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

In a recent development, that sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he mentioned: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

It has been revealed that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

It has been revealed that johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

Recent findings suggest that “They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery said. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

“Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Man Utd (A) - Oct 10th, 5.30pm.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

vs Crystal Palace (H) - Oct 31st, 5.30pm.

vs Brentford (H) - Oct 10th, 3pm.

vs Fenerbahce (H) - Oct 14th, 8pm.

vs Newcastle (A) - Oct 17th, 5.30pm.

vs Man City (H) - Oct 24th, 12.30pm.

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia highlights his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD.

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Possession: Spurs 64% vs 36% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 31 vs 18.

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

“We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we showed a really good character.”.

According to recent reports, and that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

According to recent reports, late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

Sources indicate that this will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

In a recent development, callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Industry observers note that though Savio takes the corner swiftly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

It has been revealed that maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

Kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

But it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

It has been revealed that A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

It looks like a Cash own goal...

Industry observers note that the Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye.

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher.

According to recent reports, this is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

According to recent reports, this is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

Gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

The Spurs fans are flooding out.

Sources indicate that villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

According to recent reports, gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

Marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

In a recent development, tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

According to recent reports, savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his new club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

He gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

Sources indicate that so close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

Huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Industry observers note that ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

Recent findings suggest that tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

Recent findings suggest that unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being promptly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

Savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

Industry observers note that but the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

It has been revealed that savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

We’re back in action in north London.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus.

Villa: Wan-Bissaka for Matty Cash.

And as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

In a recent development, johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

It looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

Possession: Spurs 57% vs 44% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 14 vs 11.

In all fairness to Spurs, they have pushed for a goal all half and only been denied by some fantastic keeping from Zion Suzuki.

Here are some of the biggest saves of the half:.

Zion Suzuki with a double save to deny Spurs an opener 🧤📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/b7WITUtjf2.

Sources indicate that back-to-back huge saves from Zion Suzuki! 🤯📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/uXKkicEeer.

In a recent development, predictably, there were boos from the home fans at half-time. That was the ninth half of Premier League football Spurs have failed to score in. They should have done and would have done if it weren’t for the heroics of Zion Suzuki in the Villa goal. Manzambi’s goal was only Villa’s second in the League this season and this is the first time they have led in a League game.

Spurs looking shaky now as they come close to conceding a second, seconds before the whistle finally blows.

According to recent reports, boos around the stadium as the players head down the tunnel. De Zerbi has work to do.

Spurs have not come from behind to win since November 2024.

This is a tall challenge now, as van Hecke is the first to go into the book for a foul on Jackson.

To rub salt in the wound, Spurs have a decent shout for a free kick on the edge of the box before that as Gomes pushes Mateus Fernandes as he makes a run into the box.

Well this is the last thing Spurs would have wanted. Minutes before half-time Manzambi puts the vistors in front.

Robertson slides to try and stop a ball going out for a corner but he only finds McGinn. He sends it into the box and finds Kamara, who takes a shot. It bounces towards goal and Manzambi pokes it past Kinsky for the lead.

Sources indicate that van de Ven is off the pitch on his feet, sporting an impressive bruise now. Spurs are down to 10 as they try to get the swelling down.

There will be five minutes added, though play is yet to resume as van de Ven receives treatment for a cut below his eye.

The last thing Spurs need now is to be forced into another defensive change after losing Porro.

Wan-Bissaka picks up the ball sent out to him on the wing by Manzambi, who is fouled by Marmoush.

The free kick is outside the area, but McGinn takes looking goalwards.

Recent findings suggest that good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side presently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

According to recent reports, there has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

It has been revealed that but before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club.
  • According to recent reports, juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

According to recent reports, juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he remarked, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

Sources indicate that the new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit revealed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

It has been revealed that the financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

Recent findings suggest that the offer involves up to 208.5m latest shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering newly introduced players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

Tech Report: Pocognoli's problems are just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to those running the show at the SFA

💡 Key Takeaways

  • For anyone with anything resembling a retentive memory, the alarm bells were going off all over the shop on the day Sebastien Pocognoli was unveiled as the new Scotland head coach.
  • Scottish Football Association (SFA) chief executive Ian Maxwell and chief football officer Craig Mulholland were there to crow about an extensive search of foreign fields to rival Captain Cook’s journeys around the Pacific and how data had helped land ‘one of Europe’s most sought-after coaches’ and secure the ‘aggressive, front-foot style of play’ that was going to bring a desired freshness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 10:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:25 EST, 20 November 2026.

For anyone with anything resembling a retentive memory, the alarm bells were going off all over the shop on the day Sebastien Pocognoli was unveiled as the new Scotland head coach.

Scottish Football Association (SFA) chief executive Ian Maxwell and chief football officer Craig Mulholland were there to crow about an extensive search of foreign fields to rival Captain Cook’s journeys around the Pacific and how data had helped land ‘one of Europe’s most sought-after coaches’ and secure the ‘aggressive, front-foot style of play’ that was going to bring a desired freshness.

According to recent reports, it was impossible to avoid the elephant in the room, though. Two-and-a-half months earlier, ahead of the disaster zone that was the World Cup, they’d handed Steve Clarke a fresh four-year contract.

He was the polar opposite to Poco. Aggressive and front-foot, he most certainly wasn’t. The SFA knew Clarke didn’t have it in him to go for it at a major finals – as evidenced by two separate European Championship failures – but they decided to stick with the status quo anyway. Just as they did after Euro 2024, when he should have been sacked.

When Clarke finally did go of his own accord after the summer’s events in North America, Maxwell stated he was ‘sad’ the former Kilmarnock manager had stepped down and put a major dollop of blame on ‘some fairly hysterical commentary back home’.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland,  Pocognoli and SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell.

It just didn’t add up. How do you go from thinking a guy like Clarke is the future to tearing everything up, drafting in a London-based analytics firm to tell you who to go for as his replacement and coming up with a 39-year-old Belgian who wants to go for broke?

‘It doesn’t matter how you get there,’ offered Maxwell. ‘Let’s not get too hung up on the whys and the what-ifs.’.

Unfortunately, people are now starting to get hung up over the fact Pocognoli, for all the good on his CV, looks like he’s in the wrong movie – with his refusal to break from a failing three-at-the-back strategy suggesting a diploma from the Wilfried Nancy School of Intransigence ought to be on that resume too.

They are getting hung up on the fact captain Andy Robertson came out after the thrashing from Switzerland’s B-team to reveal the mood inside the camp has changed and warn there’s no breathing space to sort this out.

And they are getting hung up on the fact that it’s becoming considerably easier to reach the conclusion those above all of them at the very top of the SFA have never had a proper grip on things at all.

Clarke, of course, only exacerbated those concerns in September by expressing the view at a public event that Maxwell and Co ‘panicked a little bit’ in giving him that incomprehensible long-term deal because he’d threatened to announce he was quitting before the finals unless an agreement was reached.

Sources indicate that ‘I wanted to control my narrative,’ he explained. It was hard to know who emerged from those admissions looking worse.

Clarke’s off the plot now, though, and it’s Maxwell, Mulholland and the SFA president Mike Mulraney left to try and convince us all that there is some kind of rhyme or reason to it all.

Industry observers note that how things shape up with Pocognoli is an acid test for them. The rise or fall of a Scotland manager always hogs headlines. Yet, it is only one of a number of things coming together in what is starting to feel like a bit of a perfect storm.

Not so long ago, Maxwell and Mulholland were also yakking plenty about their statement project to increase game time for Scotland-eligible Under-21s.

Industry observers note that it’s already in tatters, by the looks of things. The looks were watered down last month, without anything like the same fanfare, to involve Under-23 players and the intended votes on the proposals were pushed back.

In a recent development, A number of Premiership sides haven’t warmed to it and it remains to be seen whether it goes to a vote at all. Certainly, the radical change the top brass envisioned isn’t going to happen and that can only be regarded as an indicator that these guys running the game aren’t capable of taking it with them.

The start of Sebastien Pocognoli's reign has been concerning for Scotland fans.

Dundee manager Steven Pressley’s intervention over recent days hasn’t helped them either. After a long period on the outside looking in, Scotland have turned out in three major tournaments in the last five years.

That has raised many millions of pounds, but the effect on elite level is questionable. Pressley talked of the sport being ‘built on sand’ as a result of there being no kind of national facility and you’d better believe it gained traction.

Industry observers note that ‘It indicates a lot about our strategy, our longevity and our long-term vision and we are finally seeing the effects of that. We have shown none of that over the period and it is all horribly catching up with us,’ he stated.

The SFA do own Hampden, of course, thanks to that peculiar £5million deal from 2019 that involved Willie Haughey and Sir Tom Hunter ponying up half the money. Yet, how distant those days of Maxwell talking about taking examples from the way VfB Stuttgart revamped the Mercedes-Benz Arena and potentially implementing them in Mount Florida seem now.

Recent findings suggest that everyone appears to have given up on making the National Stadium better. Other problems have overtaken that old chestnut. Refereeing isn’t good enough. VAR isn’t up to scratch. General facilities require considerable improvement.

Should this Youth Strategy fail, there may also be a need for the SFA to look deeper within when addressing the dearth of top-tier talent coming through.

Recent findings suggest that it’s OK to blame clubs, but what about the level of coaching – and coach education – that exists at the national association? That’s before we even get to the ‘massive lack of expertise and education’ at the younger end of grassroots raised by St Mirren boss Craig McLeish.

According to recent reports, the SFA set-up for producing coaches was once the envy of many. We all remember Jose Mourinho and others at the Largs finishing school. Now? Even Maxwell, after stating there were no viable Scottish rivals to Pocognoli for the Scotland job, admitted the coaching pathway needs looked at.

There is only one problem here, though. Maxwell has been the chief executive since May 2018. He’s in his ninth year in the role. What has he really achieved? What have his big ideas been?

Yes, Scotland made it back to major finals under Clarke, but Clarke was a painfully obvious choice to be made national coach in 2019. He’d worked wonders at Rugby Park and did transfer that to the international scene until it came to actually turning out in those showpiece competitions.

Now they’ve had to get creative, there is so much hanging on Pocognoli’s reign for the guys at the top.

According to recent reports, maxwell was a bloke who landed in the role of Partick Thistle GM almost by mistake after failing to beat Jackie McNamara to the manager’s job. Just before leaving for the SFA, the Jags got relegated.

Talk of redeveloping Hampden has gone quiet as other problems take the spotlight.

At his Hampden unveiling, he had to fend off questions about only getting that position through behind-the-scenes politicking and insist he wouldn’t be a puppet for anyone.

Sources indicate that mulholland also seems a surprising choice as the architect of the national sport’s renovation. He spent two decades in the Rangers academy and eight years as head of it.

Has it been a conveyor belt of talent for the Ibrox first-team? Do you recall much wailing and gnashing of teeth when he left in 2023 amid a wider changing of the guard?

Then, there’s Mulraney, the former Alloa chairman and SFA director for over a decade.

It has been revealed that you don’t see much of him these days. Maybe because people want to ask about his position as chair of FIFA’s finance committee in the wake of the most greed-infested World Cup ever and the ongoing soap opera surrounding Gianni Infantino. But maybe not.

How things work out with Pocognoli might end up being the one thing that puts all these guys under the kind of examination that cannot be bodyswerved, but it’s only the tip of the iceberg.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adrien Rabiot heaped praise on Goncalo Ramos for what he does for the team, but he also explained what AC Milan’s ‘problem’ is.

Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1. Gabriele Calvani’s own goal put the home side ahead, before Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted to make it a rout.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is a third consecutive league victory after the wins over Inter and Genoa and it moves the Rossoneri on to 27 points, back inside the Champions League places. Up next: a trip to Athens to face Olympiacos on Thursday in the Europa League, and a chance to demonstrate consistency.

After the full-time whistle, Rabiot spoke alongside Ramos to both Sky and DAZN, offering his thoughts on what was a very successful evening in front of all the fans at San Siro. His words are via MilanNews.

Are you starting to build a good identity?

“Our problem is that we have to be focused for 90 minutes. We did well today, even though we conceded a bit at the end, but that’s normal. As I said, we’re growing as a team: the quality of our play, the team spirit, the sacrifice for 90 minutes, and everyone.

Recent findings suggest that “Gonçalo is the first to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very crucial player for us, and we have a lot of games: I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit. But everyone’s attitude was great today, and we have to keep it up.

“In these last few games, when we play like this, when we’re so focused and manage to do what we work towards in training, I think we’re all enjoying ourselves, even tonight. We created a lot, we scored a lot of goals. What we have to focus on is enjoying playing together.”.

Why didn’t you shoot before the first goal?

In a recent development, “I wanted Pulisic to score, but the defender came back rapidly. It’s true that I could have shot, but I get more pleasure from providing an assist than from scoring. But I did the assist afterwards.”.

“He does a great job. Not everyone understands it, but he does an incredible job. When we get in and score, it’s also credit to us. Then we feel happy when he scores, also because it gives him confidence. Good for us and for him, for everyone.”.

Barcelona's quest for another Champions League crown continues when they face Sabah at Baku Olympic Stadium on Wednesday.

Despite sitting top of the La Liga table, Hansi Flick is dealing with numerous problems, including on the injury front.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Barcelona's injury and suspension news ahead of their clash with Sabah.

Espart is out for at least another month or so due to an ankle injury; the youngster faces a battle to be unavailable before the winter break in Spain.

Bardghji was expected to leave Barcelona on loan during the summer transfer window before the news broke that he had suffered a torn ACL, which will sideline him for a significant period.

Possible return date: December 2 (vs. Atletico Madrid).

Rodri sustained a hamstring injury during the team's Champions League clash against Aston Villa on November 3, but he could be back on the field in early December.

It has been revealed that possible return date: November 24 (vs. Sabah).

Barcelona confirmed that Andreas Christensen has some discomfort in his left calf, which resulted in him missing his side's clash with Villarreal on November 22, though he has not been ruled out of his side's next Champions League game.

Barcelona have no players banned for this match.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

Sources indicate that he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

According to recent reports, it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

In a recent development, “It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Sources indicate that any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

According to recent reports, “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola stated. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

In a recent development, isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Recent findings suggest that “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola stated, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

Recent findings suggest that one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

It has been revealed that “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose said. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola noted: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

It has been revealed that jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that showed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

"Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y.

Industry observers note that "That's a massive moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39.

Cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young said on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose substantial players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.

Fair play to anyone who retained Brobbey in their Fantasy Football teams this week...

It has been revealed that andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

In a recent development, his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

In a recent development, everything Iraola has stated and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

Sources indicate that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has stated that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

According to recent reports, adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He remarked: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his major move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, noted: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:25 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:32 EST, 20 November 2026.

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada insists the team got 'fundamentally better' after this summer's transfer window, as he warned ‘spending just for the sake of it’ is not the route to putting United back on top.

In his first sit-down interview in five months, Berrada tackled topics ranging from the relationship between the Glazers and Ineos, the imminent departure of youngster JJ Gabriel, the decision not to sign a left back in the summer, as well as the decision to push ahead for a new stadium despite supporter backlash on matchdays.

The United chief has been at the centre of furious protests and anti-ownership chanting at matches this season, alongside Director of Football Jason Wilcox, and he accepted that criticism of United's leadership has, mostly, been fair.

In an interview that aired shortly after latest head coach Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time, Berrada was pressed on how much accountability falls at his door with United heading to Anfield this weekend 18th in the Premier League table.

'I think if you think about the fact we've had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven't achieved the stability that we wanted, that's for sure,' Berrada told Sky Sports.

'When it doesn't work out with the coach or the manager, we are all responsible. Myself, the football leadership, everyone who is involved around the coach and the staff and the players. We have to continue improving and getting better.

Manchester United's CEO Omar Berrada finally fronted up in an interview with Sky Sports.

Michael Carrick's sacking was yet another managerial change at United, with the hierarchy under massive scrutiny and Mauricio Pochettino now in the hotseat.

'There are different circumstances why it didn't work out with Erik [ten Hag], and Ruben [Amorim], and now Michael [Carrick], and we are always learning and, as I remarked, trying to improve and understand what has failed.

'The challenge is we're trying to find the right manager for the squad that we have with a specific set of skills in that moment to make them perform at their best level.

Sources indicate that 'It's true, we have to accept the criticism that we haven't been able to achieve that stability with one coach and our aim is to do that as soon as possible. Of course, we hope now that Mauricio coming in will give us that stability that I think we all need.'.

Berrada's links to Manchester City, where he worked prior to joining United, were brought up, not least given he worked at the club during the period that City have had charges brought against them.

'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted.

But at his latest home there are issues aplenty, not least having got another managerial appointment wrong, sacking Carrick less than six months after handing him a two-year deal, and so it was put to Berrada: is the club actually progressing?

'It's not good enough, not acceptable and that's why we've made the change that we made so that we can move forward,' he concluded.

(L-R) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Berrada and Jason Wilcox have drawn plenty of ire from Man United fans.

Sources indicate that 'But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth, to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. It's not always been that.

'Last year we finished third, we were happy with the squad, we were happy with the way we were going. And now, a few months later, we are not where we need to be. But the foundations are there and I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction. Very positive.'.

According to recent reports, sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

Industry observers note that on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

According to recent reports, "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville claims Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

It has been revealed that neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

In a recent development, it begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

In a recent development, we now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

Sources indicate that that still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

Industry observers note that that 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

According to recent reports, the goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

In a recent development, this stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

According to recent reports, fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

Bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa.

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces.

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

According to recent reports, fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

Industry observers note that the interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

Fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

Sources indicate that bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

United have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

Fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

It has been revealed that promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

If Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia.

It has been revealed that subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe.

Here's how The Fulham shape up. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/0IxS0J3ldf.

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊.

It has been revealed that the script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick notes Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a substantial impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager mentioned.

“That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty massive one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

Recent findings suggest that “But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

The mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and latest head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Recent findings suggest that fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

Industry observers note that moise Kean has suffered a fresh tibia injury in training with Como. The former Juventus striker is now undergoing further medical tests. Sky Sport Italia reported that he will be out for about two more months. That timeline rules him out of Como’s home game against Juventus.

Recent findings suggest that como’s statement of 17 November gave no recovery date. The club promised an update once more information was available.

The upcoming problem follows a treatment that was meant to end his shin trouble. On 30 October, Como’s update described his treatment at the Cugat Institute in Barcelona as successful. The club put his recovery at about five weeks. His progress was to be reviewed every day.

The setback is a heavy blow for Como. In Serie A, his outings for the club added up to 160 minutes. He has yet to score, including in his single Champions League game. He joined from Fiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent. At Fiorentina he scored 27 league goals in two seasons, 19 of them in 2024/25. Before that, he came through the Juventus academy.

According to recent reports, without him, Como will have to rely on Douvikas up front. The club may also look for a striker in January.

For Juventus, the news removes one threat from a crucial stretch. Como are their next opponents after Venezia. The game is the Sunday evening fixture a week later, in round 13 of Serie A. Kick-off is at 20:45.
