Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (720 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that high intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work.
  • Across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often.
  • The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that high intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work. But a new study suggests that for women, it can also lead to worse treatment from colleagues.

Across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often. Men with high scores did not receive such treatment, and in one group, they were treated better.

The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.

According to recent reports, since it was published this year, Nitya Chawla, an associate professor at UCL School of Management in London and the researcher behind the study, says women have written to her saying the findings matched their own experience at work. Some told her they had wondered whether they were to blame for hostility.

Sources indicate that the researchers ran two studies. The first followed 432 business students at a US public university working in small teams on a consulting project for real organizations. The second surveyed 394 full-time employees working in teams at a financial manufacturer in China.

Intelligence here means cognitive ability measured with a standardized test of reasoning and problem-solving that employers use in hiring. Teammates were not told of anyone's scores. They rated one another, and a few weeks later each person reported how much help they had received and how often they had been undermined, for instance by having information withheld.

The effects were small, and the study highlights a link, not proof that colleagues' perceptions caused the treatment. Participants reported help and mistreatment themselves, and the study did not look at race or ethnicity.

In the student group, the difference between women and men was no longer statistically significant when two participants with extremely low scores were included.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The researchers point to social role theory, the idea that people expect men and women to fit traditional roles: men as capable and assertive, women as warm and supportive. A woman with high cognitive ability breaks that expectation, and colleagues may assume she lacks warmth.

"It's that automatic, implicit assumption that takes place alongside the presence of intelligence that then drives these more negative interpersonal behaviors," Chawla told DW.

It has been revealed that in both groups, women with higher scores were rated as more hostile. Among the employees in China, they were also rated as less warm. Women seen as more hostile reported less help, both with their work and on a personal level, and more undermining.

In a recent development, the team also checked whether the women were simply behaving differently. Higher-scoring women were rated as somewhat more domineering, but that did not explain why they received less help or more mistreatment. The findings point to colleagues' assumptions, Chawla claims, rather than to anything the women did.

It has been revealed that no, men with high intelligence scores do not face the same treatment. Among the students in the United States, a man's score made no difference to how his teammates rated or treated him.

Sources indicate that among the employees in China, men with higher scores were rated as less hostile, received more help and were mistreated less often. The authors suggest the difference between the two groups may reflect cultural differences in gender norms, but they did not test this.

Industry observers note that no, Chawla states. "That would be really the wrong conclusion to draw.".

Small effects still matter, she argues, because they are experienced day after day. Over time, this kind of treatment can lead to anxiety, self-doubt and a sense of not belonging. "These experiences and these feelings can become very, very burdensome over time," she said.

Chawla puts the responsibility on workplaces rather than on women. Managers, she indicates, should track how team members treat one another, and organizations should hold regular check-ins to see whether employees are getting equal support.

Individuals can ask themselves a simple question, she indicates: would they react the same way if that colleague were a man?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • "It was clear to us from the outset that the analysis would uncover uncomfortable truths," Defence Minister Boris Pistorius of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) told theBundestag, Germany's lower house of parliament, on Wednesday.
  • Earlier that day, he had presented the findings of the Bundeswehr's first study into unreported cases of sexual misconduct to the Defense Committee.
  • "The study has shown that only between one third and one sixth of cases are reported," Pistorius mentioned, announcing an action plan to address the glitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"It was clear to us from the outset that the analysis would uncover uncomfortable truths," Defence Minister Boris Pistorius of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) told theBundestag, Germany's lower house of parliament, on Wednesday.

Earlier that day, he had presented the findings of the Bundeswehr's first study into unreported cases of sexual misconduct to the Defense Committee. According to the findings, sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr is far more widespread than previously known.

"The study has shown that only between one third and one sixth of cases are reported," Pistorius mentioned, announcing an action plan to address the glitch.

Sources indicate that "There is zero tolerance for sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr. This is nothing less than a matter of upholding the human dignity enshrined in our Basic Law. And that principle applies all the more within the Bundeswehr.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The study examined incidents that had gone unreported, the so-called "dark figure" of cases that never reach official statistics. The Bundeswehr Centre of Military History and Social Sciences (ZMSBw) surveyed 45,000 service members, around 18% of whom responded. More than 8,100 questionnaires were evaluated and supplemented with individual and group interviews. According to the institute, the data are statistically representative.

Industry observers note that according to the study, younger women in the lower ranks are particularly affected by sexual misconduct. Among men, non-heterosexual soldiers are disproportionately affected. The perpetrators are predominantly male. Statistically, combat units do not differ from the rest of the armed forces.

Female service members in units with a higher proportion of women (more than 15%) are less likely to be affected.

In a recent development, verbal harassment is by far the most common form of misconduct, according to the study. Around 72% of female soldiers and 31% of male soldiers mentioned they had experienced verbal harassment at least once during their military service. In the 12 months preceding the survey, 38% of female soldiers and 16% of male soldiers reported experiencing verbal sexual harassment.

For physical harassment, 9% of female soldiers and 3% of male soldiers reported incidents of physical sexual misconduct, and 2% of both women and men remarked they had experienced sexual violence.

The study also examined why service members chose not to report incidents. The most commonly cited reason was not wanting to draw attention to themselves.

Sources indicate that "There appears to be a lack of awareness of the reporting channels. And, for me, the decisive matter is trust in those channels," Pistorius concluded.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In response, the Bundeswehr looks to improve awareness of how and where cases of sexual harassment can be reported. That is precisely where the environmentalist Greens, who are in opposition in the Bundestag, direct their criticism.

Defense policy spokesperson Sara Nanni is calling for "an external reporting office, alongside the regular disciplinary process, with investigative powers and the authority to take disciplinary action where appropriate." Such an independent point of contact, she argues, is needed in cases where superiors within the Bundeswehr fail to fulfill their responsibilities.

In a recent development, another consequence of the study is the expansion of support services for those affected. A counseling center established in early November will soon be available around the clock. Supervisors are also to receive enhanced awareness training and improved instruction.

"Sexual misconduct will become part of training at every level, from the very beginning," remarked Bundeswehr Inspector General Carsten Breuer.

In addition, the way supervisors handle reported cases will become a standing criterion in their performance evaluations. "Anyone who fails to lead by example, tolerates misconduct, or does not address it consistently will no longer hold a leadership position," Defense Minister Pistorius stressed.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the study was prompted by a growing number of reports of sexual misconduct received by former Parliamentary Commissioner for the Armed Forces Eva Högl. Most of those who approached her were female soldiers. Högl called for the study into unreported cases in 2024. The process gained further momentum following incidents at the Parachute Regiment in Zweibrücken that came to light at the beginning of this year and also involved allegations of sexual misconduct.

The current Parliamentary Commissioner for the Armed Forces, Henning Otte, described the figures revealed by the study as "dramatically high." The findings had also made it clear, he said, "that there is a lack of trust in the Bundeswehr's structures. The Ministry of Defense must now take this study seriously and translate its findings into a leadership culture that is truly lived in practice.".

Industry observers note that the Bundeswehr urgently needs additional personnel and has been actively recruiting women. However, the study's findings are unlikely to make attracting more female recruits any easier. Women remain significantly underrepresented across nearly all branches of the armed forces.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:21 EST, 21 November 2026.

Cristiano Ronaldo may have finally departed the international stage, but he still remained a major part of Portugal's story over the past week.

That came after they suffered a humiliating 4-1 defeat by Denmark in the first game since his retirement, their heaviest home loss in competitive history.

In the aftermath of that match, Ronaldo's mother Dolores launched a furious and unprompted attack on the national team, claiming the defeat was just, and added she was happy to see the result.

Despite an emotional and historic tribute to Ronaldo pre-game, Dolores also expressed her unhappiness at what had unfolded, before she claimed the veteran's former international team-mates failed to show him the respect he deserved during his career.

Dolores has not always been an outspoken presence over the years, but has often stepped up to defend her son when she feels necessary.

So, in light of her outburst, Daily Mail Sport has taken a look at other examples of when the mums of footballers have got involved in their careers.

Cristiano Ronaldo's mum became embroiled in her son's row with Portugal's national team after saying she was happy to see them suffer a heavy defeat (Source: Instagram/doloresaveiroofficial).

Veronique Rabiot – Adrien Rabiot.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique has developed a reputation as an uncompromising and fiercely protective negotiator in her role as his agent.

This has seen the French midfielder face several flashpoints in his career, beginning  when Veronique pulled him out of Man City's academy after just six months in 2008 because she felt they were not looking after his interests like they should be.

During his time at PSG, where Rabiot ultimately broke through and spent seven seasons in the first team, Veronique then frequently clashed with the club's hierarchy.

Potential transfers to Roma and Man United during his career have also both collapsed late on, a factor some reports attach to Veronique's role in the deals.

There have been several notable flashpoints on the international stage too, not least when she backed her son's controversial decision to withdraw from France's standby list for the 2018 World Cup.

But that was nothing compared to the aftermath of France's shock exit from Euro 2020 at the last-16 stage.

Veronique made headlines at the time for engaging in a heated confrontation with the parents of Kylian Mbappe and the entourage of Paul Pogba in the stands over on-pitch errors and perceived arrogance during Les Bleus' campaign.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique (centre) has developed a reputation as a formidable force.

As the mother of one of the best footballers on the planet, Fayza Lamari was always likely to be a major powerbroker, and she has played a key role in Kylian Mbappe's career, acting as his chief negotiator and business manager.

This has seen Fayza oversee Mbappe's commercial obligations and image rights, while she played a central role in his dramatic contract extension at PSG in 2022.

She was similarly key when Mbappe joined Real Madrid in 2024. On that occasion, she was credited for helping to secure a huge signing bonus and favourable image rights split for her son.

Fayza hasn't been afraid to publicly stand up for the forward, and she was key in the legal dispute over unpaid salary and bonuses that he felt he was owed by PSG after his exit.

PSG were ultimately ordered to pay Mbappe €60million (£52.5m) by a French court in a major victory for Fayza.

Kylian Mbappe's mum Fayza (also pictured with his brother Ethan) has played a key role in the commercial side of his career.

Sheila Ebana has been a foundational and supportive presence throughout Lamine Yamal's childhood and rise into professional football.

But, alongside regularly attending Yamal's games, Sheila has become a celebrity in her own right after embracing her public profile.

She regularly provides an insight into her life and shares behind the scenes clips with Yamal and his half brother Keyne on social media, racking up 2.8million followers on Instagram and 2.6million on TikTok.

Sheila has also regularly made paid appearances and attended VIP events, including a bizarre Christmas gala dinner that Daily Mail Sport went to in November 2025 where members of the public paid hundreds of pounds for a three-course meal, champagne, entertainment and a meet-and-greet.

To demonstrate how Sheila has embraced her fame, she once responded to online critics by retorting: 'I don't just think I'm famous - I am.'.

Lamine Yamal's mum (pictured below together with his half-brother Keyne) has embraced her celebrity fame.

Denise Bellingham – Jude Bellingham.

Jude Bellingham has often credited his mother Denise for helping to manage his life off the pitch and keep him grounded.

When he moved to Germany to join Borussia Dortmund as a 17-year-old, Denise went with him – before subsequently following the midfielder to Spain after his transfer to Real Madrid – while his father Mark stayed with his brother Jobe.

She is understood to handle his domestic affairs and finances, while Bellingham inadvertently revealed during the 2022 World Cup that she still made his bed.

Denise has generally provided a constant source of advice, logistical support – which has included driving him to training in the past – and organisational help throughout his time in the game.

The England star is clearly appreciative of all she has done, describing her as his 'queen' and 'backbone', and crediting her with helping to keep him level headed throughout the highs and lows of his career.

Jude Bellingham (pictured also with dad Mark and brother Jobe) has described his mum Denise as his 'queen' and 'backbone'.

Marcia Lewis – Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mother Marcia Lewis has played a crucial role in his rise into Arsenal and England's first team.

When Lewis-Skelly entered the Arsenal academy system at the age of eight, Marcia wanted to learn more about football to ensure she could protect and guide her son's progression.

She subsequently qualified as an agent, meaning she now represents Lewis-Skelly, and also enrolled in a Master's degree in Football Business.

Marcia has since taken part in contract negotiations and filtered external pressures away from her son during his development.

She was later inspired to set up the No1Fan.club, a platform that aims to support families who have children in academy football.

The outlet is dedicated to helping navigate various challenges that arise, such as dealing with scouts, agents and the general pressures associated with youth football.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mum Marcia Lewis tried to learn more about the business of football so she would be able to support her son on his journey (Source: Instagram/myleslewisskelly).

Harry Maguire's mother Zoe has taken a more low-profile approach to her son's career than others, yet she has never been afraid to speak out when she feels the need to.

This included back in 2023 when she snapped after years of watching her son face significant abuse, both online and in stadiums.

At the time, Zoe labelled the heat on the defender as 'disgraceful' and 'unacceptable', and noted it went 'far beyond' football.

She re-emerged into the public eye three years later when Maguire was snubbed from England's World Cup squad.

After that, she tweeted: 'Absolutely disgusted.'.

According to recent reports, in another post addressing Maguire, she added: 'You couldn’t have done anymore. Hold your head high …Disgraceful.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

Recent findings suggest that but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

For Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

According to recent reports, keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews stated. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

Recent findings suggest that brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

According to recent reports, it was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very vital points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

Industry observers note that an encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola noted they will now be out “for some time”.

Recent findings suggest that the loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

It has been revealed that the injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their massive-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa noted: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

Luxury automaker Mercedes-Benz is halting investment at its facilities in Germany, a board members announced on Thursday.

Mercedes-Benz is "forced to examine, in concrete and detailed terms, which sites in Germany we can still afford to maintain," board of management member Britta Seeger stated in an interview published on the manufacturer's intranet.

Germany's major IG Metall trade union has enabled the possibility of longer warning strikes amid difficult negotiations for industrial employees.

"The board of IG Metall has pave the way for 24-hour warning strikes in the metalworking and electrical industry," the union stated on Thursday.

The union accuses employers of intransigence after three rounds of negotiations without clear progress.

On Wednesday, regional chapters appealed for authorization for full-day warning strikes — the last step before a full union vote and an indefinite labor dispute.

"This escalation is completely excessive and counterproductive," Udo Dinglreiter, the president of the employers' umbrella organization, Gesamtmetall, stated. He said that hundreds of thousands of jobs could be at risk.

IG Metall's first chairperson Christiane Benner countered that "the employers want to turn this round of collective bargaining into a dispute over principles." Another union official said they were offering what amounted to a real-terms pay cut rather than seeking solutions.

IG Metall is calling for a 5% pay increase and other improved conditions for some 3.7 million workers starting in November, while employers have offered a one-off payment in 2027 coupled with a 1.3% increase starting in the summer of 2028.

The union estimates that around 464,000 employees took part in the initial wave of warning strikes that were limited to periods of hours, rather than full days.

Employers argue that they're treading a difficult line between trying not to cut jobs and meeting calls for improved pay amid widespread industrial sector layoffs in Germany in recent years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, 'Tis the season, already. Preparations are underway around Germany and in several cities, Christmas markets are opening to the public.

Some markets are already open in Essen and in Hamburg, Duisburg's opens on Thursday, and Cologne's follows a day later.

The coupons.de website has sought to track the planned prices for mulled wine or Glühwein as the markets open their doors nationwide.

The bad news? These prices are rising like so many others. The better news? The year-on-year increase is actually smaller than overall inflation figures, at around 1%.

On average, a cup is liable to set you back around €4.60 (roughly $5.10). Not entirely surprisingly, Munich tops the nationwide pricing chart, with the price peaking at €7. Other sites nationwide tend not to have the gall even to charge 6 euros.

Bargain hunters determined to get the best value mulled wine will need to venture deep into the center of Germany — hardly its core tourist hub — to find the lowest prices starting at around €3.50.

Deposits for the cup, the "Pfand," are also only going in one direction, and in the meantime range from €1 all the way up to €5. But there's a strong argument, particularly with the better designs or after a memorable trip, that this can be money well spent as a memento!

Police in the Emsland region in the northwest near the border to the Netherlands have reported a major fire in a complex of residential and commercial buildings in Papenburg.

The fire broke out on Wednesday afternoon, police said the following morning, causing damages worth "at least €10 million ($11 million)." Several hundred emergency services personnel were deployed.

"Based on current findings, the fire broke out in the sauna area of a gym facility on site, and quickly spread to further parts of the complex of buildings," police wrote.

Two men were in the sauna at the time and initially tried to douse the flames but without success.

Police mentioned the buildings were evacuated as the fire spread, with some surrounding buildings also being cleared as a precaution because of possible smoke-related dangers.

Several people were injured, police mentioned, including the two men in the sauna area suffering mild burns and suspected smoke inhalation sickness. They were treated in a nearby hospital but soon discharged.

"There were also injuries among the first responders," police wrote. "Four police officers, two firefighters and members of the rescue teams suffered mild injuries, particularly via smoke inhalation.".

According to recent reports, the fire was only extinguished late on Wednesday night, several hours after it started. The area is sealed off, with possible risks of damaged buildings collapsing. Police have also released investigations into the fire's cause, but said that at present, the area was not safe for that work to start at full scale.

Germany's largest credit bureau Creditreform has published its "2026 Debtors' Atlas.".

It finds that 10.16% of German adults, or 7.36 million people, exhibit at least the early warning signs of excessive debt. A year ago the ratio was 9.74%.

"The financial situation of private consumers has further deteriorated," Patrik-Ludwig Hantzsch, Creditreform's head of economic research, mentioned. "In particular, the sharply increased living costs, energy costs and housing costs are straining expenditures.".

Hantzsch stated employment was also becoming an glitch once more, saying "above all, well-paid jobs in manufacturing industries have been cut back in large numbers in recent months.".

The report also highlights rising cases of signs of excessive debt prior to legal action being taken, such as payment reminders or warnings being sent, saying "consumers are taking on more credit-financed expenditures — increasingly also for smaller purchases — at simultaneously rising interest rates.".

A larger share of men than women have excessive debts, perpetuating a longstanding trend.

People around the middle of their working lives, aged 30-39 and 40-49, are most likely to be affected — but the cohort with the fastest-rising share of people with excessive debts are young adults below the age of 30.

Bremen, Berlin, Saxony-Anhalt and North Rhine-Westphalia were among the states with the highest rates of excess debts, while the wealthy and fiscally conservative states of Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg had the lowest levels.

Germany's main DAX stock market index has cleared the 27,000-point mark for the first time in its history in morning trading.

It climbed by around 1.3% in order to pass the milestone.

A combination of some positive outlook data from major companies, not least engineering giant Siemens, and the falling oil prices of recent days have helped fuel the uptick.

Siemens' shares had risen by almost 5%, to just over €291 (around $323) each, helping to spur on the gains and making the company the morning's top performer.

Despite several years of low growth and recession in the German economy, the DAX, like many Western indices, is now trading twice as high as it was prior to the COVID pandemic.

Hundreds of police officers searched apartments and meeting sites for the biker group "Gremium MC" in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg early on Thursday.

The state interior ministry mentioned the operation was part of a move to outlaw three sub-chapters of the group, the ones based in Böblingen and Leonberg, as well as the "Gremium MC Chapter Nomads Bosphorus Türkiye.".

Industry observers note that this last group was highlighted as a meaningful part of Gremium MC by security officials. It describes itself on Facebook as a great example that "people of different cultures and faiths can be strong together," featuring images of men posing with knives and other weapons.

Gremium MC prominently incorporates into its iconography the symbol of the Prussian military medal for exceptional valor, the Iron Cross, which was discontinued after World War I, reintroduced by Adolf Hitler during World War II, and then scrapped for good.

State Interior Minister Manuel Hagel was expected to make further comments later in the day in Ludwigsburg.

Gremium MC is deemed an "outlaw motorcycle gang" in Baden-Württemberg's latest security report, a term used for biker groups that do not recognize the state monopoly on the use of force and are often tied to organized crime.

"Extortion, drug dealing and pimping in particular tend to be part of their activities," state authorities say.

Baden-Württemberg counts 154 biker chapters in the state with around 2,000 members.

According to recent reports, founded in 1972 in Mannheim, various chapters of Gremium MC across the country have faced legal issues in recent years. In 2021, another chapter in the southwest, Gremium MC Southgate in Heidelberg, was outlawed on suspicion of organized crime activity.

Police in Hanover reported early on Thursday that three men were injured by an unknown driver in a car in the nearby town of Ronneberg.

One person sustained severe injuries in the incident late on Wednesday, police said.

Two of the wounded were taken to a nearby hospital while the other could be cared for at the scene.

According to recent reports, police said the driver fled the scene and that a search operation was ongoing. Authorities were also still investigating a potential motive for the apparent attack.

Today's updates start with a focus between the southwestern Kurpfalz and Swabian regions, where police have introduced major morning raids against a biker gang.

The state Interior Ministry in Baden Württemberg has outlawed three of its chapters. Hundreds of police officers mobilized in the early hours of the morning.

The major IG Metall trade union is planning further strikes in the carmaking sector and other metalworking industries, with an announcement anticipated later in the day.

To the north, near Hanover, police report an apparent car attack injuring three men overnight.

And in the spirit of offering the public service journalism people are truly thirsting for, we'll have some info on the average and localized pricing of mulled wine or Glühwein at Christmas markets this year, as the early birds start to open their doors to visitors. (Yes, already!).

  • Goalkeeper Lee and five of his Everton Under-21s teammates have gleefully taken up the task of being reading buddies to the children of Ellesmere Port’s Meadow Primary School, one of six schools that make up the recently renamed Everton Multi-Academy Trust (EMAT).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Captain Underpants”. The laughter that follows is infectious. It seems doubtful that it was an honest answer to the question posed to Zach Lee by the young boy located somewhere near the front of the classroom: “What is your favourite book?” But it got exactly the reaction he was after.

Industry observers note that the room is abuzz. It has been for much of the past hour.

Goalkeeper Lee and five of his Everton Under-21s teammates have gleefully taken up the task of being reading buddies to the children of Ellesmere Port’s Meadow Primary School, one of six schools that make up the recently renamed Everton Multi-Academy Trust (EMAT). Seven miles away, six of their Under-21 peers are doing likewise at Oldfield Primary School in Chester.

Nearer to Liverpool, the hollers that greeted Everton Women’s Holly McNamara and Karen Holmgaard 24 hours earlier are still reverberating around the corridors of Bidston Avenue Primary School.

Christian Nørgaard and close friends Tyler Dibling and Tyrique George are also familiar with the noise the pupils at the Birkenhead school can make. Last month, the trio were serenaded with a ukulele rendition of Spirit of the Blues on a visit there. Blue ukuleles, of course.

If the colour of the musical instruments is a cute indicator of the strengthening ties between the football club and the EMAT schools, the time being spared by the players is of much greater significance.

Recent findings suggest that it is intended to demonstrate a cross-Club connection with EMAT, which sits alongside Everton in the Community as one of Everton’s associated organisations. “Part of the Everton family,” as Everton’s Chief Tax and Sustainability Officer and Chair of Trustees for EMAT Alison Haynes puts it.

In a recent development, but there is a deeper intention, too. “We want to use the power of the Everton crest to inspire and engage youngsters in education,” indicates Steven Baker OBE, CEO of EMAT. Baker has seen this in evidence for more than a decade, having previously served as Principal of Everton Alternative Provision Free School, the award-winning L4 facility that offers youngsters who have struggled in mainstream schools a route back into education.

Lee and his Under-21 colleagues, McNamara and Holmgaard are all supporting one particular mission of EMAT - to inspire youngsters towards a life-long love of reading. More immediately, to ensure they have the requisite literacy level to adequately prepare them for what lies ahead in secondary school education.

In Ellesmere Port, Chester and Birkenhead, the players are tackling their role head on. Books - donated by Everton staff to help replenish the schools’ libraries - are strewn across the tables and spilling onto the floor. No-one’s troubled by the mess.

Sources indicate that julia Donaldson’s greatest hits are being played out across the room. Michael Morpurgo – a childhood favourite author of midfielder Jack Patterson – can be heard, too. ‘Bluey’ is an appropriately named hit on another table. And then there’s Lee and a group of little ones giggling at Captain Underpants.

Close by to the classroom at Meadow, Everton’s leading post-war goalscorer Graeme Sharp is here too, continuing the literacy theme by officially opening the school’s newly-refurbished library.

According to recent reports, “These children will remember today,” says Baker. “They will remember players from Everton coming into school and taking the time to sit with them.

“They love hearing stories but they also love having someone to read to. Both aspects are so important for a child’s development.”.

As is music. It’s why Dibling, George and Norgaard found themselves being taught the chords to one of Goodison’s – and now Hill Dickinson Stadium’s – favourite tunes last month.

Studies show a direct correlation between a child mastering a musical instrument and making their mark in maths and other creative fields.

The Toffees trio left behind gifts of recorders (blue ones), helping the school expand the opportunities it can offer to its pupils.

“We find it’s really key for their resilience and it's good for the children mentally and socially to have the opportunity to not only play an instrument, but to play to an audience,” claims Bidston Avenue headteacher Stuart Brady, a Tranmere Rovers fan.

“It's great for us as a school to have the connection we do with Everton and the players. Days like this are great, but it's also about the children feeling they belong to something bigger.”.

And the proof that EMAT is getting it right is stacking up. In 2024, Everton Free School and Everton Football College – the two original schools on which the Trust was founded – were jointly awarded an ‘Outstanding’ rating by Ofsted. Earlier this year, the respected national TES Awards named EMAT (then The People’s Learning Trust) as its Trust of the Year for trusts with nine schools or fewer.

With the support of a Premier League football club and its players behind them, it is hoped the collective will continue to go from strength to strength.

The intention is that Everton’s Under-21s will return to the schools to resume their reading buddy duties at junctures throughout the season, strengthening their bonds with the schools and pupils. It is seen as a vital part of the players’ professional development.

Representatives from the Men’s and Women’s team will continue to play their part also. Merlin Röhl has already been a guest of Oldfield Primary School’s after-school chess club, taking up an invitation to share his love of the ancient game with the next generation.

“We understand the responsibility and influence we have as a football club when it comes to our communities,” notes Haynes. “And you cannot understate the impact the player visits have.

“The atmosphere and the smiles you see in the room, the energy they give to the children… it’s truly wonderful.”.

Latest Update: What are fossil fuels?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (597 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life.
  • The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.
  • They started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life. But now they threaten to make the planet unlivable for many plants, animals and humans.

The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.

They started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals. When they died, they sank to the bottom of oceans and swamps where they decomposed under layers of sediment.

It has been revealed that over time, this matter was buried deeper and deeper into the earth, subjecting it to increasing pressure and heat which changed its chemical composition. Plants and trees transformed into coal, whereas microscopic plankton and algae became oil and — if the heat and pressure increased further — gas.

Today fossil fuels can be found in the earth's crust all around the world although some countries, such as the US, Saudi Arabia and Russia, have bigger reserves than others.

Coal, found in underground coal beds, is extracted by mining, whereas oil and gas, found in reservoirs beneath the land and ocean, are accessed by drilling.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since the early 19th Century, when the discovery and exploitation of fossil fuel reserves powered the Industrial Revolution, our use of them has skyrocketed, increasing eight-fold since 1950.

Today they provide 80% of our energy needs through heating, electricity generation and transport.

We transform them into energy either by burning them directly in furnaces that warm up our homes and businesses, or in power plants to heat water into steam which then generates electricity. When it comes to transport, crude oil is refined into a range of products such as diesel, gasoline and kerosene that are burned in the engines of automobiles, airplanes and ships. Natural gas is also sometimes compressed for use in cars and buses.

But fossil fuels are also essential to a huge range of products including steel, formed using a coal-derived material called coke, and plastic, which is produced by refining and processing crude oil and gas.

Recent findings suggest that fossil fuels are by far the biggest contributors to climate change. When burned to power our modern lives, they emit carbon dioxide (CO2) into Earth's atmosphere, trapping heat and causing temperatures to rise.

With 2025 officially one of the warmest years on record, the impact of these emissions is being felt around the world. Hotter temperatures are causing polar ice caps to melt and creating the conditions for extreme weather events — such as floods, drought, wildfires and storms — to become more intense and frequent.

Scientists stress the need to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) to avoid unleashing the most catastrophic impacts of climate change. That was laid out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. Right now, there are 194 parties to the agreement, but progress has been too slow, and overall emissions continue to rise.

Three years after countries agreed at the UN climate conference in Dubai COP28 to transition away from coal, oil and gas. After the previous COP in Brazil failed to reach a consensus on a concrete blueprint, Brazil has now presented a roadmap aimed at turning that promise into national aims.

"It is long past time to stop treating the transition away from fossil fuels as taboo or intractable," United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres remarked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By FABRIZIO FERRARI FOR DAILY MAIL SPORT.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 05:49 EST, 21 November 2026.

Not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone. It is a town of 42,000 best known for many years as the birthplace of 20th-century screen icon Marcello Mastroianni and global hotelier Carmine Forte, but now the talk of Italian football.

Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, currently above Juventus and Napoli in the table.

Armed with the second-lowest budget in the league, they have regularly started with seven Italian players – the most in the league – including Antonio Raimondo, a 22-year-old striker on loan from Bologna, who scored nine goals in 10 appearances before being halted by injury at the start of this month.

The majority owner is Latest York investment fund Clara Vista, who are part of the consortium behind Ipswich Town, and the head coach is Massimiliano Alvini, who has drawn comparisons to Roberto De Zerbi for both the high-intensity elements of his style and his rise from the humble depths of Italian football.

Only 18 months ago, in May 2025, they looked set to slide into the third tier, bound for a relegation play-off until Brescia were deducted points to hand Frosinone an unlikely stay of execution.

It has been revealed that A month later a fresh sporting director, Renzo Castagnini, arrived and installed Alvini, who kept faith in most of the squad that had survived only by the skin of its teeth. Survival was again the sole aim. Yet from the very first Coppa Italia fixture Frosinone began to turn heads, beating Monza, a team widely tipped for promotion.

According to recent reports, by the end of the season, they had finished as runners-up behind Venezia and above Monza who were promoted via the play-offs. It was Frosinone’s fourth promotion to Serie A and by far the most beautiful because nobody saw it coming.

Massimiliano Alvini was recognised as the best coach of Serie B at the 35th edition of the FIGC Panchina D'Oro Awards on Monday.

Frosinone Calcio players celebrated their victory against Lecce in October.

Much of the credit belongs to Alvini, who was named by his fellow managers on Monday as Serie B’s best coach for 2025-26. The 56-year-old Tuscan played at an amateur level until a serious injury forced him to quit at 30. His coaching career began in the same lowly ranks for Italian football.

Recent findings suggest that he and his brother Walter sold shoe soles for a living. Increasingly, Walter would be asked to cover at work as his brother followed his upcoming passion, travelling to study the training sessions of established coaches, including Luciano Spalletti at Roma and Maurizio Sarri at Empoli.

Alvini remains grounded and stubbornly modest despite eight promotions and the sudden spotlight.

If the season ended today, Frosinone would qualify for Europe but perhaps the most incredible part of the story was improvements made last season by individual players who had barely registered in the previous season.

Industry observers note that notably Fares Ghedjemis, who went from scoring two goals to 15. Also Castagnini signings such as Giacomo Calo and others including Giorgi Kvernadze, Gabriele Bracaglia and goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani.

Frosinone won 3-0 at Fiorentina, beat Cesc Fabregas’s Como 2-0 and Torino by the same score. At Atalanta – the Europa League winners of 2024 now managed by Sarri – they drew 4-4 and came within a whisker of a late winner.

Twenty points from the first ten games recalled the early bursts of Claudio Ranieri’s newly promoted Fiorentina in 1994-95 and Juventus in 2007-08.

Industry observers note that then, in the last fixture before the international break, came a third defeat of the season, at home against Cagliari, despite 29 shots and 13 corners. One of those days when the ball simply refused to go in.

According to recent reports, whether the shareholders of Clara Vista – which bought 80 per cent of Frosinone in the summer – are entirely delighted remains to be seen. There have been suggestions they hoped to see more of the 13 players signed via their data algorithms but only Patrizio Masini and Romano Schmid have been regular starters.

The other nine or 10 names regularly in the starting XI are the same men who drove the climb out of Serie B.

Defensive midfielder Giacomo Calo has scored five goals in 11 games this season.

Sources indicate that when it comes to the metric of ‘passes per defensive action’, a key indicator of how quickly the ball is won back, Frosinone rank among the top four clubs in Europe. The others are Barcelona, Brighton and De Zerbi’s Tottenham.

Still, Alvini shrugs off the praise. His first seven years as a coach produced two promotions, one sacking and one relegation. Then a group of friends decided to start a club in the seventh tier (the third amateur level) and put him in charge.

In the seven seasons from 2008 to 2015, Tuttocuoio climbed via four promotions into Serie C.

According to recent reports, alvini moved on to fresh challenges. The next four seasons at Pistoiese and AlbinoLeffe brought his first two professional sackings. He lists them openly on LinkedIn, almost as badges of honour, albeit the second was not a conventional dismissal.

Emergency surgery to insert an artery stent early in the season left him psychologically raw when he returned.

According to recent reports, those three years at AlbinoLeffe however proved formative because he was able to watch Gian Piero Gasperini’s Atalanta methods at close quarters. He took that inspiration into the following campaign at Reggiana, taking them back to Serie B after 21 years for his seventh promotion.

Frosinone supplied the eighth and his second taste of Serie A. The first came when he was tempted from Perguia to Cremonese with a team simply not equipped for a relegation scrap. He was sacked by January.

The return is proving sweeter than he could have dared to imagine.

Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.
  • In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
  • The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.

The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.

Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors.

The New York Times first reported that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

Later Thursday, Reuters news agency alleged an intimate relationship between Huang and a second employee, citing unidentified sources.

In a recent development, those revelations emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The woman, Alice Huang — no relation — is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that runs artificial intelligence (AI) data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia.

The US government is investigating the startup on suspicion that it secretly sent some of its Nvidia chips to China, violating Washington's curbs on high-end semiconductors.

Those advanced Nvidia processors ‌are ​used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products.

Megaspeed denies the allegations and on Thursday pledged to cooperate with US investigators. Huang, the alleged spy, has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan — a key chipmaking island.

While Nvidia's board backed its CEO after the first scandal emerged, market watchers believe the second caused too much reputational damage to one of the world's top three companies by market value.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang doesn't believe in formal succession planning, so with little notice, Nvidia appointed CFO Kress as interim CEO.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is working with advisers to identify potential permanent successors.

Kress, other senior Nvidia executives and members of Huang's own family have been mooted as replacements. The family members include his daughter Madison, a senior director of product marketing, and his son Spencer, who presently works in the firm's robotics division.

Rumors also abound over a longer-term solution. On India's CNBC-TV18, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld from the Yale School of Management floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook and ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

US President Donald Trump also backed Cook on social media, writing: "A Legend replaces a Legend.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The scandals have certainly hit Nvidia's market value. Since the first extramarital affair emerged on Sunday, the chipmaker's market capitalization has fallen by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion.

Nvidia shares were down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday, after dropping by 10% earlier this week. Some analysts expect the stock price to struggle in the short term.

Nvidia stock hit all-time highs just a month ago as US technology giants continued to announce billions in spending on AI infrastructure.

Demand for Nvidia's advanced chips is so high, however, that many market analysts expect little impact on near-term sales.

"While Jensen [Huang] is the heart and lungs of the Nvidia story…the company and its leading-edge GPU technology will go on and [his departure] does not change the entrenched position Nvidia has in the AI Revolution chip arms race," said Dan Ives, a partner, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, a US-based merchant bank.

Analysts see the biggest long-term risk in strategy and execution. After all, Huang was the leader who picked which ideas Nvidia should bet heavily on and got the whole firm behind them.

His sudden exit is also seen as highly disruptive to the chip designer's strong relationships with AI hyperscalers, Taiwanese chip producer TSMC and foreign governments — especially China.

Huang was Nvidia's main lobbyist on US chip export rules and persuaded US President Donald Trump to ease some curbs on China last year.

Huang is often called a rockstar CEO for his leather jackets instead of suits.

Like Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, he was also seen as a key-person risk as Nvidia’s public image, strategic direction and technical decisions became closely tied to him.

Huang steered the company for more than three decades and was also respected for his hands-on involvement in product architecture and engineering decisions.

He also insisted on a flat management structure, with around 60 executives reporting directly to him.

Huang has run the organization so tightly around his own technical judgment and product decisions that investors may have little sense of how it would function without him.

According to recent reports, at the same time, Nvidia is no longer the startup Huang founded in 1993. The company has built deep expertise in chip design and software, creating a durable moat that helps protect its huge profits, which topped $120.1 billion last year.

Some analysts argue that its central role in the AI hardware buildout makes it less dependent on Huang’s day-to-day input.

China is quickly playing catch-up with the US in the global race for AI dominance.

While Chinese AI models have lagged behind the likes of ChatGPT and Claude, recent updates from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot have closed much of the gap on benchmark tests and often beat US rivals on cost and speed.

Beijing is also investing heavily in domestic chips and data centers to reduce reliance on US hardware.

The US has curbed exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips.

However, this move has only slowed the pace of China's AI ambitions.

Reuters reported Thursday that Chinese AI firms are now trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, amid fears the US could further tighten restrictions on advanced chips.

Also Thursday, Beijing accused the US of using the Nvidia spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on China.

The concern is likely to dominate talks next week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen in southern China.

Fans attending Everton Women’s game against Brighton & Hove Albion this Sunday have the opportunity to win a fantastic range of prizes – simply by tapping their phone!

Ahead of the Barclays Women’s Super League game at Goodison (2pm GMT kick-off), supporters can ‘check in’ digitally via a dedicated stand located in the Gwladys Street concourse for a chance to have their matchday upgraded to one of our VIP lounges.

An additional ‘check-in’ point will also be located next to the refreshment kiosk in the small courtyard inside turnstiles 1 & 2 of the Main Stand, located between the Main Stand and Park End.

Once you have scanned the dynamic QR code on your mobile device*, you’ll be automatically directed to a page to fill in your details for a chance to win this, and other exclusive prizes. These include a chance to take part in the half time ‘Hit the Bar’ challenge on the hallowed Goodison turf, a post-match meet and greet with an Everton Women’s player and free tickets and upgrades for the festive fixture against Arsenal on Friday 11 December**.

NB: Winners will be contacted via text message ahead of kick-off.

And as fans at Goodison familiarise themselves with the latest technology, watch out for further prizes and discounts at future games.

*Anyone over 18 attending the game can scan the dynamic QR code.

**U14s must be accompanied by an adult.

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been seen in public for the first time since the tragic accident.

During a match earlier this month, Andorra keeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out Tenerife star de Miguel with a high challenge which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

De Miguel's passing shocked the footballing world and Owono was subsequently given a 12-match ban by authorities.

Both sides have been back in action since the tragedy, but on Friday, Andorra hosted Leganes at their Estadi de la FAF.

That was their first home game since de Miguel's passing, and they made sure to pay a moving tribute to him on the night.

Before the match, the players went onto the pitch wearing shirts with his name and number on them and they carried out a bouquet of white flowers.

Andorra keeper Jesus Owono was seen in public for the first time since Jesus de Miguel's tragic death as he attended a tribute to the former Tenerife star.

Before Andorra's game with Legannes, several tributes were paid, including a minute's silence.

A minute's silence was also held before the game, while those in attendance applauded during the ninth minute of the match, the shirt number worn by de Miguel at Tenerife.

The most striking part of the evening though was Owono's attendance in the stands.

The goalkeeper has stayed away from the public eye since de Miguel's death, after which he was subjected to chants of 'murderer', but he wanted to attend the tribute at his club's home ground.

Owono was wearing a black coat and hat as he stood next to team-mates who weren't involved in the matchday squad.

Despite receiving the support of the crowd and his team-mates, local reports said Owono cut a downcast figure and that he was seen praying immediately after the minute's silence.

Owono's desire to attend the tribute came after he had also asked to meet de Miguel's family, something he hopes to do one day.

Meanwhile, Tenerife returned to action last week against AD Ceuta CF in a match that was also filled with tributes.

Players provided a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – another nod to de Miguel's shirt number.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars then took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the tragedy.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of de Miguel before the game kicked off.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

It has been revealed that other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, de Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place de Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

Owono was watching the game from the stands as he stood next to some of his team-mates.

Tenerife returned to action last week and paid several tributes to their former star de Miguel.

The tragedy occurred as the game between Tenerife and Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when de Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for his side in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, de Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

Owono's 12-match ban is currently in effect, yet his manager Carles Manso hinted that he may never play again.

He said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two Iranian men were found guilty of spying on dissident journalists in Britain on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Thursday.

British counterterrorism police said the case reflected intensifying hostile Iranian activity in the country, an glitch that recently made headlines amid the security scare at the RAF Fairford airbase that's a major operational site in Europe for the US Air Force.

The men, both in their 40s, were arrested last year, with Iran repeatedly rejecting the allegations against them.

The Woolwich Crown Court in London convicted one of the Iranian citizens not just of spying on journalists working for the Persian-language dissident TV channel Iran International, but of plotting a violent attack against one or more of them.

The second individual had also faced charges of plotting an attack but was only convicted of spying on the reporters.

One of the convicted defendants mentioned he was acting under duress after his family was threatened, and the other said he did not know that his actions were assisting Iranian intelligence.

A third defendant, a 57-year-old Iranian man, was acquitted of all charges.

The men were accused of engaging in conduct likely to assist the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Iran's multi-discipline military force that's seen as closer to the country's religious leadership and more influential than its regular armed forces.

The UK formally designated the IRGC as a threat to national security in July, meaning that supporting or assisting the organization can carry penalties of up to 14 years in prison as part of fresh rules on national security and state threats.

Sentencing in this case is still pending and is scheduled for mid-December.

"This was a calculated operation to spy on those critical of the Iranian regime," stated Frank Ferguson, chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service's special crime and counter-terrorism division.

The two men were accused of visiting addresses linked to their targets, taking photos and videos, and using platforms such as ChatGPT to research them online.

"Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place," prosecutor Ferguson noted.

Senior ‌National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing Vicki Evans said that the IRGC or "middlemen" for Iranian intelligence were directing the plot.

Iran's government had repeatedly denied the allegations, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying he was "disturbed" by the trio's arrests last May.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

There have been four cases targeting the Persian language television channel Iran International since late 2023.

In July, two Romanian men were jailed for stabbing a journalist outside his home in 2024.

A spokesman for the broadcaster's parent tech giant, Volant Media, mentioned in a statement that Thursday's verdicts "don't make the lives of our journalists any safer so long as the Islamic Republic of Iran continues its campaign of death threats and violence against them.".

Iran International reported that a British barrister was also one of the targets.

British law enforcement has been warning of an uptick of hostile Iranian activity in recent years, particularly since the US military operations against Tehran began earlier this year.

Most notably, the UK has accused Iran of being behind a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford base in September, after which US President Donald Trump withdrew some long-range bombers from the site.

Three men were indicted in the US in relation to that plot this week, while two others right now face charges in the UK.

It has been revealed that but beyond this, the head of Britain's MI5 domestic intelligence agency Ken MacCullum noted in October that Iran-linked operations had led to more than 50 arrests in the last year. He also said known cases of so-called state threats had more than quadrupled in a decade.

Counter-terrorism police chief Evans noted she expected this trend to continue.

France this week also accused Iran of being behind a cyberattack targeting refrigeration units at hundreds of supermarkets in October, although Iran denied any involvement.

European governments are on heightened alert for so-called hybrid warfare tactics, from Russia as well as Iran, amid the geopolitical tensions of recent years. Latest technologies like low-cost drones and AI are also threatening to make such activities cheaper, harder to trace, and potentially more effective.

#128902. Microbiome home tests are taking off. Can they be trusted?
